name_reason: Complies with data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention. 'chapter_event_handler_3a' is the consuming handler's dispatch index (0x3A is a domain ID, not a Ghidra address residue). 'pickup_item_id_table_inline' reflects the data type (item-id lookup table, inlined into the function). No hex address residue (no suffix equals own address 0x5274e or a target). Name accurately reflects both purpose and array data type.
purpose: Inline 5-byte const lookup table mapping tile terrain-class index (0..4) to the item id granted by the tile-pickup chapter event handler (dispatch idx 0x3A).
logic_summary: 5 const bytes { 0x1D, 0x2B, 0x33, 0x3D, 0x47 } copied into a local at handler entry, then indexed by the cursor tile's terrain-class byte to pick which item the pickup tile hands out. Each entry is the class-best ultimate weapon for one job line: 0x1D 戰神戟 (knight), 0x2B 魔神斧 (warrior), 0x33 風神弓 (archer), 0x3D 光之杖 (priest), 0x47 魔龍爪 (samurai). All five are AP-400 items tagged '最強武器' in the item KB. Only reader is fd2_chapter_event_handler_3a__ch26_pickup @ 0x354fe (ch26's live 5-box treasure pickup, reached via tile_pickup consequence 0x3A dispatched by menufld.c).
element_semantics: Each byte is an item id (range 00h-D6h) granted for the corresponding tile terrain-class index. [0]=0x1D 戰神戟/knight-best, [1]=0x2B 魔神斧/warrior-best, [2]=0x33 風神弓/archer-best, [3]=0x3D 光之杖/priest-best, [4]=0x47 魔龍爪/samurai-best. Reader adds +0xB5 to derive the dialog sprite id.
notes: Verified data bytes via read_memory (1d 2b 33 3d 47 = exactly 5 bytes, then zero padding). Item ids cross-checked against fd2-knowledge skill (all five = class ultimate weapons, AP 400, '最強武器' tag) -- source comment claim confirmed. Only xref is READ/DATA from the single consuming handler; zero write-xref => genuinely const (matches src 'static const'). Source comment block (lines 486-518) already accurate, precise, ASCII+permitted Chinese item names; left unchanged. Ghidra has no plate on the data address itself; the consuming-function plate @ 0x354fe describes the table consistently (5-byte item-id lookup by tile attribute), so no plate edit needed. Out-of-bounds read caveat (terrain class > 4 reads raw stack frame) is a pre-recorded issue on the consuming function (emit_issues 000354fe), not a new finding for this global; no src/logic change made per refine rules.
